messages:
alex: ok team — starting the SDK publish window in ~5m. plan: staggered empirical rollout instead of full dist-tag flip. :eyes:
maria: what do you mean by empirical rollout? sounds fancy :)
sam: gist — start canary (5% traffic), monitor errors and perf metrics for 30m, bump cohorts on green. fallback = rollback to previous dist-tag and pin users if we see regressions.
alex: exactly. goal is to avoid full-cutover surprises after last-minute test regressions. will use deploy-bot to tag and assign cohorts.
maria: do we still do a soft deprecation note for the legacy sync client in this window? legal asked for 48h heads-up before removing docs links.
jeff: we can post a deprecation blurb but hold actual yanks until next window. for today's publish only: pin older major as "legacy" dist-tag and stop auto-redirects.
alex: agree. nina can you draft the short deprecation paragraph and add to release notes?
nina: on it. draft: "Note: legacy sync client (v1.x) is deprecated; we will continue to serve it for 90 days while encouraging migration to the v2 async client. See migration guide: <https://redwood.dev/migrate-sync-to-async>"
sam: quick ops checklist I ran locally before canary: ```
# publish commands
npm run build && npm publish --tag canary
python -m build && twine upload dist/* --repository pypi-canary
```
sam: deploy-bot pls start canary tag when ready. :pray:
deploy-bot: publish job queued by sam. job id: pb-20290314-77. will report back with artifact checksums and smoke-test logs.
devex-oncall: running smoke tests against canary artifacts now (auth, basic generate, embed). ETA ~8m.
(8m later)
deploy-bot: pb-20290314-77 finished. npm canary tag published: @redwood/sdk@canary-20290314. checksums: sha256:abc123... smoke-tests: ok (3/3).
sam: smoke looks good. rolling to cohort 1 (5%). routing rule applied: feature-flag sdk_cohort=canary1 -> canary tag.
maria: monitoring dashboards? which panels we watch?
jeff: errors/slo, unit token latency p50/p99, embed mismatch rate (for embedding change), and canary-specific evals (fuzz on top prompts). set alerts at +3 sigma from baseline for 10m window.
alex: if any alert fires we immediately flip routing to previous dist-tag and start rollback playbook. rollback criteria: >1% error delta OR p99 increase >50% OR embedding regressions >2%. agreed?
maria: agreed. also add manual opt-out: any engineer can @devex-oncall to pause ramp.
nina: release notes updated with deprecation text and change log snippet. will push to docs site after final canary green.
sam: cohort metrics look steady after 40m. error delta 0.2%, p99 +8% (within threshold). bump to cohort 2 (25%).
deploy-bot: routing rule updated. cohort 2 live.
(another 20m)
devex-oncall: all green. no alerts. embedding regression test passing.
alex: thanks. schedule: hold full dist-tag flip for end of change window (quiet hours 02:00-04:00 UTC). if no regressions by then we flip `latest` to new version and soft-deprecate legacy dist-tag.
jeff: small ops note — for Python we must ensure packaging metadata keeps the legacy entrypoint for one more minor to avoid import breakage. patch a compat shim if needed.
maria: can we add an npm dist-tag pin for enterprise customers that requested no-canary behavior? they want explicit pinned versions.
sam: do `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@2029.3.14-enterprise enterprise` and share in sales channel. also add the pinned wheel artifact to the internal artifact registry.
deploy-bot: enterprise dist-tag added as requested.
alex: docs and release notes live?
nina: pushed. release notes: <https://redwood.dev/release/2029-03-14> includes migration guide, deprecation notice, and rollback instructions.
jeff: follow-up actions: (1) cut a hotfix branch template for fast rollback, (2) add automated post-flip smoke test that runs across all regions, (3) confirm k8s routing TTL is 30s so flips take effect quickly.
maria: logging: include canary cohort id in telemetry events (`sdk.cohort = canary1|canary2|prod`) so we can slice easily.
sam: tagging is done. I'll watch overnight and @channel if anything noisy. thanks everyone :rocket:
